title: Tube laser cutting machines
subtitle: Senfeng T, PLUS, GPLUS / GT, NT and ST tube and profile fiber lasers · Ø0.4″ to 25″ · 20 to 40 ft · 1.5 to 20 kW
cover_line: Senfeng Laser · made in China · sold & serviced in Canada by NovoTech
about_title: Round, square and profile tube cut to length with every hole, cope and notch in one pass
about_text: A tube laser cuts round, square, rectangular and open profiles to length and cuts the holes, copes, slots and notches in them in one pass, straight from the 3D model — no saw, no drill, no notcher, no layout. The T series two-chuck machines cover Ø0.5 to 14″ and 20 to 40 ft with 1.5 to 6 kW; the PLUS series runs to 492 ft/min and 240 rpm on small tube; the GPLUS / GT cut ±45° bevels for weld preparation; the NT three-chuck machines cut the last part without a tail; and the ST three-chuck machines carry tube to Ø25″ and 6,614 lb over 30 to 40 ft with 6 to 20 kW sources, for structural steel, towers and trailers. Every machine can be loaded by hand, or with a semi-automatic or a fully automatic loader.

Senfeng Laser has built fiber laser machines in Jinan, Shandong, since 2004: a 1.8 million ft² campus, its own laser sources, cutting heads and welding guns, around 15,000 machines a year, 20 overseas branches and Senfeng Laser USA with a warehouse and service team. CE, FDA and ETL certified and CSA approved. NovoTech sells, installs and supports the machines in Canada from Mississauga, ON, Canada — layout for your building, installation, operator training, a CSA-approved panel, a 1-year warranty and parts and technical support in Canada.
made_in: Made in China by Senfeng Laser — CE, FDA and ETL certified and CSA approved

intro_pages.title: Which Senfeng tube laser? The five series side by side
intro_pages.lead: The number of chucks decides what is left of each bar and how heavy a tube the machine carries; the chuck size decides the largest tube; the loader decides how much of the operator's time each bar takes. Each series has its own pages further on, with the full specification table of every model.

paras: The all-round two-chuck machine and the first tube laser of most shops: 1.5 to 6 kW, Ø0.5 to 14″, 20 to 40 ft bars, fifteen models on 20, 23, 24.6, 30 and 40 ft beds.

Tuned for speed on small and medium tube — 492 ft/min and 240 rpm chucks, 3 to 6 kW — for furniture, fitness equipment, racking and automotive parts cut by the thousand, with a very short to zero tail.
Two chucks and a 3D head that tilts ±45°, so mitres, chamfers and weld preparations are cut in the same pass as the holes: the GPLUS for Ø0.6 to 4.7″, the GT for Ø2.3 to 14.1″.
A third chuck takes over the bar as it shortens, so the last part is cut with zero tail — several percent of material saved on every bundle of 20 to 40 ft stock, Ø0.7 to 14.1″, 3 to 12 kW.
Three heavy chucks carry pipe, large tube and structural sections to Ø25.1″ and 6,614 lb over 30 to 40 ft without sag, with 6 to 20 kW sources; semi-automatic loading and unloading are included.
intro_pages.note: Ranges are for the series; each model's chuck size, bar length and weight are in its specification table. Tail: the piece of each bar that a two-chuck machine cannot cut because the rear chuck holds it.

intro_pages.title: Loading the tube: by hand, semi-automatic or fully automatic
intro_pages.lead: Every tube laser in this catalogue can be loaded three ways. The loader does not change what the machine can cut — it decides how much of the operator's time each bar takes, and whether the machine keeps cutting while nobody stands at it.

cards.title: By hand or crane — no loader
cards.text: The operator lifts each tube onto the infeed supports — by hand for light tube, with a hoist or crane for heavy bars. The rear chuck pulls it in, the chucks centre and clamp it, the following supports carry it and the machine cuts the whole bar on its own; the finished parts drop onto the unloading rack.
items: Standard on the T, PLUS, GPLUS / GT and NT
The lowest price and the shortest machine
Any profile the chucks hold — angle, channel and special shapes too
Right for short runs, mixed jobs and light tube

cards.title: Semi-automatic loader
cards.text: The operator lays a row of tubes on the loader's sloped rack or chains and keeps it filled; the loader separates one tube at a time, lifts it to the chuck centre and feeds it in. A tube outside the loader's size or weight is still loaded by hand.
items: Sloped loader: 17 – 20 ft (5.2 – 6.2 m) tubes up to 265 lb (120 kg) — round, square, rectangular and channel
Dual-arm chain loader: 13 – 20 ft (4 – 6.1 m) tubes up to 529 lb (240 kg) — also angle, channel and I-beam
Chain loader: 13 – 40 ft (4 – 12 m) tubes and profiles up to 1,543 lb (700 kg)
Takes special shapes and open profiles that a bundle loader cannot; included on the ST

cards.title: Fully automatic bundle loader
cards.text: The crane sets a whole bundle — up to 3 t (6,600 lb) — into the loader; it separates the tubes, aligns each one and feeds it to the chuck with no operator, while the unloading system sorts the parts from the scrap. One person runs the machine and prepares the next bundle while it cuts, and the machine keeps cutting through breaks.
items: Fully automatic loader: 11.5 – 20 ft (3.5 – 6.1 m) tubes, 15 – 30 ft (4.5 – 9 m) on the 9 m machines
Simplified fully automatic loader: the same 3 t bundle on a lighter frame, also for 20 – 40 ft (6 – 12 m) tubes
Round, square and rectangular tube of standard section, 265 – 573 lb (120 – 260 kg) per tube
The choice for production runs and two-shift work

intro_pages.note: Unloading: a 6.6 ft (2 m) unloading rack that sorts scrap from parts is standard on the T and PLUS (10 or 13 ft optional) and a 10 ft (3 m) unloading system on the NT (20 ft optional); the ST comes with semi-automatic loading and unloading. The loader for each model is listed in its specification table.
